fact: Togo First says Togo AI Lab, led by the Ministry of Public Service Efficiency and Digital Transformation with CEGA at Berkeley, is recruiting a technical lead to oversee machine-learning, generative AI and satellite-imagery tools for sectors including agriculture, health, education and the environment.

Togo-Presse reports the minister of Economy put the Digital Market Intelligence platform, built by SICPA, into service on 12 March 2026, using AI and data analysis to detect suspicious transactions and fraud and smuggling, run from a command centre staffed by tax, customs and commerce services.
The Togo Data Lab is developing with the Ministry of Agriculture a project using satellite images, ground data and AI for farmers, not yet reported in service.

Sika Finance reports the economy minister officially launched the AI-based Digital Market Intelligence platform, which cross-checks tax-marking and inspection data to give inspectors predictive indications of risk zones.
Sika Finance reports an announced precision rate of 89.89% for the Digital Market Intelligence platform.

Togo's government used machine learning on mobile phone and satellite data under the Novissi emergency cash transfer programme to target vulnerable households, paying about $20 a month to 154,238 people between December 2020 and April 2021.
Researchers at UC Berkeley's CEGA found the machine-learning targeting improved accuracy by 42% compared with a simpler method based on the poorest districts.
